title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #1
body: Ask how many cheques the rent is on. Twelve cheques is survival. Four is comfortable. One cheque, paid in January, is the answer you're looking for, and they will say it like it's nothing. If you hear "we're in Marina" that's good, "Downtown" is better, "Dubai Hills" means the family moved here to stay. It's a sealed deal if the villa is in Emirates Hills and they describe it as "a bit far."
caption:
Tip #1 😭 "one cheque" is the whole flex.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #2
body: Ask about the visa and watch the whole thing reorganise. "I'm on my company's visa" is an employee. "I'm on my own visa" is a business. "We have the Golden" is a different conversation entirely and they will mention it within nine minutes. It's a sealed deal if nobody in that family has thought about a visa renewal in five years.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #3
body: Watch where they shop for groceries, because in Dubai that is the entire class ladder. LuLu is home. Carrefour is fine. Spinneys is comfortable. Waitrose in Dubai Mall for four items is a statement and everybody knows it. It's a sealed deal if they say "just get it from Waitrose" about something that costs nine dirhams at LuLu.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #4
body: Ask what they did on Saturday. Brunch is the marker and the venue is the tier. Bla Bla and Zero Gravity is the young crowd. Nikki Beach is trying. A table at a hotel brunch that was booked by someone's assistant is the real one. It's a sealed deal if they've been going to the same brunch every month for four years and know the manager's name.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #5

The real answer is Ravi in Satwa at midnight, sitting on a plastic chair, and every Pakistani in this city has done it. It's a sealed deal if a family with a villa in Dubai Hills still drives to Satwa for karahi and considers that completely normal.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #6
body: Ask about summer, because July sorts this city. Everyone complains about the heat. Only some people leave for two months. "We do London in summer" or "the kids and I go back, he stays" is the tell, and the flights were booked in February. It's a sealed deal if somebody has spent eight consecutive summers out of the UAE and calls it going home.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #7
body: There are two lobbies and you keep aiming at the loud one. The rented Lamborghini on Sheikh Zayed Road and the JVC apartment with the ring light is not it. The real one is a family in a Dubai Hills villa driving a Patrol, kids at Dubai College, nothing posted anywhere. It's a sealed deal if the surname is on a trade licence older than the person you're talking to.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet Your Rich 🚩 Spouse in Dubai. Tip #8
body: Ask how long they've been here, because it's the quiet hierarchy. "Two years" is new. "I was born here" is a whole different person, and they will say it flatly, and everyone at that table recalculates. Their father came in 1994 with nothing. It's a sealed deal if they remember what Sheikh Zayed Road looked like before the Marina existed.
